lines.text:
A Tour of the Fire Station

Our school organised a trip to the local fire station last week. The firefighters were friendly and showed us everything.

The station has a large garage where the fire engines are parked. Each truck carries hoses, ladders, axes, and first aid equipment. The firefighters explained that a fire engine can carry over a thousand litres of water in its tank.

We saw the firefighters' uniforms hanging in a row near the garage: helmets, fireproof jackets, heavy boots, and breathing apparatus. They told us they can get dressed in under sixty seconds when the alarm goes off.

Upstairs, there is a common room where the crew rests between calls. It has a kitchen, a dining table, and some sofas. Next to it, there is a dormitory with bunk beds for night shifts. When the alarm sounds, the firefighters slide down a pole to reach the garage quickly.

The station also has a training tower where firefighters practise climbing ladders and rescuing people from height. Outside, there is a yard with a practice area for using hoses and extinguishers.

The fire chief gave us a talk about fire safety. She explained the importance of smoke alarms, fire exits, and escape plans. She showed us how to use a fire extinguisher: Pull the pin, Aim at the base, Squeeze the handle, and Sweep side to side — the PASS technique.

At the end of the visit, we got to sit in a fire engine and turn on the siren. It was an exciting and educational day.

lines.text: Welcome to the fire station! I'm the fire chief. This is where our firefighters live and train.
lines.name: Welcome to the fire station! I'm the fire chief. This is where our firefighters live and train.

lines.text: Is that a fire engine? It's huge!
lines.name: Is that a fire engine? It's huge!

lines.text: That's our main fire truck. Next to it is the ladder truck for tall buildings, and the water tanker for areas without a hydrant.
lines.name: That's our main fire truck. Next to it is the ladder truck for tall buildings, and the water tanker for areas without a hydrant.

lines.text: What about the ambulance and the helicopter?
lines.name: What about the ambulance and the helicopter?

lines.text: The ambulance is for the paramedic team. The helicopter and the rescue vehicle are used by the rescue team for big emergencies. We even have a fire boat for the harbor.
lines.name: The ambulance is for the paramedic team. The helicopter and the rescue vehicle are used by the rescue team for big emergencies. We even have a fire boat for the harbor.

lines.text: Can we see the equipment? I want to see the fire hose!
lines.name: Can we see the equipment? I want to see the fire hose!

lines.text: Of course. Here's the fire hose with the nozzle, the fire extinguisher, and the ladder. The axe and the pike pole are for breaking through walls.
lines.name: Of course. Here's the fire hose with the nozzle, the fire extinguisher, and the ladder. The axe and the pike pole are for breaking through walls.

lines.text: What do firefighters wear? That helmet looks heavy.
lines.name: What do firefighters wear? That helmet looks heavy.

lines.text: This is the turnout coat, the fire boots, and the gloves. The face mask and visor protect our eyes. And this is the breathing apparatus with the oxygen tank.

lines.text: The thermal camera — it sees heat through smoke. The radio keeps us connected to the dispatcher, and the siren tells everyone we're coming.

lines.text: 'Firefighter' is the modern, inclusive term used officially in the UK and US. 'Fireman' is outdated. Many fire services actively recruit people of all genders.

lines.text: UK law requires smoke alarms on every floor. Carbon monoxide detectors are required near gas appliances. Fire blankets are recommended in kitchens. These vocabulary items appear in safety leaflets.

lines.text: November 5th is 'Bonfire Night' or 'Guy Fawkes Night' in the UK. People light bonfires and set off fireworks. Fire safety advice is widely shared every autumn.
